review.centralDecision: The logarithmic map is an L2 isometry. Nonnegativity permits Tonelli before finiteness is known. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds every translation correlation and the exponentially decaying positive kernel has finite beta mass. Unit-norm long interval indicators have triangular correlations converging pointwise to1, with the kernel as an integrable majorant. Thus the exact bound is sharp. Equality forces translation defects to vanish for almost every nonzero shift; even one such shift makes a nonzero L2 function periodic, impossible. Strong continuity extends the stated argument to every shift. This is a complete sharpness/nonattainment proof, not just a formal candidate eigenfunction.

review.author: root
review.centralDecision: The logarithmic map is an L2 isometry. Nonnegativity permits Tonelli before finiteness is known. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds every translation correlation and the exponentially decaying positive kernel has finite beta mass. Unit-norm long interval indicators have triangular correlations converging pointwise to1, with the kernel as an integrable majorant. Thus the exact bound is sharp. Equality forces translation defects to vanish for almost every nonzero shift; even one such shift makes a nonzero L2 function periodic, impossible. Strong continuity extends the stated argument to every shift. This is a complete sharpness/nonattainment proof, not just a formal candidate eigenfunction.

review.centralDecision: Negative eigenvalues do not exclude finite-time amplification; optimize the largest singular value of the full flow over time and initial direction.
review.nearestNeighbor: Distinct from Floquet growth: the system is autonomous and asymptotically stable, while the requested quantity is its finite-time operator-norm maximum.

review.difficultyRationale: The seven potential Olympiad menus include the actual norm at t=1, which survives elementary lower and upper bounds; deciding against it requires the time-optimization step.
